subject: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:

- Goals: reduce tail latency for user-facing scoring in US/EU, ensure EU data residency for EU customers, and have predictable unit economics vs current hyperscaler setup.
- Current infra: you mentioned a mix of Vertex for embeddings and SageMaker endpoints for generation; you’re observing occasional spikes in tail latency during traffic bursts.

Key differentiators we discussed (brief):
- Smart routing across regions with policy-based fallbacks (keep traffic in-region when required).
- Automatic prefix/KV caching to cut token costs for repeated prompts.
- Dedicated capacity options for predictable throughput and isolation vs shared hyperscaler endpoints.

Proposed next tests / action items:
1) Red team will run a comparative latency sweep across US-East (us-east1) and EU-West (europe-west1) against your current SageMaker/Vertex baseline (we’ll instrument p95/p99 and tail-burst behavior).
2) We’ll provide a short test-config.yml and a CSV template for results ingestion so you can compare apples-to-apples (attached: performance-run-20260512.csv).
3) Send us any data residency constraints or DPA items so we can confirm our Private deployment options and DPA clauses (link to our DPA: https://redwood.ai/legal/dpa).
4) Schedule a 30m technical test kickoff with your infra lead (suggested: Thu or Fri this week).

Attachments: performance-run-20260512.csv

Would you prefer Thu 10–11am PT or Fri 2–3pm PT for the test kickoff?

Thanks — looking forward to running the head-to-head.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up

Thanks Jordan —

Appreciate the recap. Thu/Fri both could work; leaning toward Thu 10am PT. A couple of notes from our side before the kickoff:

- We ran a quick baseline against our current AWS setup (SageMaker + VPC endpoints) last week — saw ~80ms median and p95 around 240ms under a small burst workload. We’ll send the PDF with the raw figures (attached). Would be useful if you can target p95 < 150ms in the US and similar in EU.
- EU availability is critical for a subset of our users due to GDPR/data residency — we need confirmation that requests and logs for EU-marketed customers can be kept in EU-only regions (and a clear list of what’s stored outside).
- Can you share SOC 2 or other compliance paperwork ahead of the kickoff? Our legal team (Priya) will review.

Attaching: baseline-aws-results.pdf

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alex.rivera@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up

Alex —

Great, Thu 10am PT is confirmed. Calendar invite sent.

Pre-kickoff notes / what we’ll bring:
- A short playbook (attached: redwood-multi-region-playbook.pdf) that shows our recommended test harness, traffic profiles, and how we measure p50/p95/p99 across regions.
- A light-weight test script that we’ll run from your infra (or we can run with a short VPN connection) to capture tail-burst behaviour.
- SOC 2 + compliance pack will be shared via secure link before the call (we’ll also include a DPA pointer: https://redwood.ai/legal/dpa).

What we need from you before Thu:
- The baseline PDF you attached is perfect. If you can also share a short example payload and the list of EU-only customers (or a sample tenant ID) so we can scope the residency test that’d be ideal.

Next tests after kickoff (plan):
1) Baseline replay in US-East + EU-West (our infra will mirror the traffic shape you provide).
2) Run model variant comparisons (quantized vs fp16) to show unit-cost / latency tradeoffs.
3) If the residency requirement is strict, we’ll propose a Private deployment or region-only routing config and surface cost delta.

Attachments: redwood-multi-region-playbook.pdf

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FintechCo - Multi-region performance follow-up

Ethan / Sean —

Forwarding the thread with FintechCo (Alex/Priya). Kickoff Thu 10am PT. Quick asks ahead of the call:

1) Can you prep the test-config.yml we discussed (include region pins for us-east1 & europe-west1, traffic shape file, and KV cache disabled for the first run)? I attached the initial config we’d use (test-config.yml).
2) Confirm what we can state re: EU data residency (what logs/meta are retained outside region for hosted API; include fallback behavior if a region is down). If a Private option is needed, include rough T-shirt cost delta for a dedicated EU pool.
3) Pull SOC2 attestations + compliance pack and upload to the secure link so I can share with Priya before the call.

Attaching: test-config.yml (template)

Thanks — Jordan
